Owner Takes His Cadillac Escalade-V to a Tuner, Goes Home With 800 Horsepower
10 photos
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube
For some car owners out there, stock just doesn’t cut it. They need to go beyond the factory standard. That's exactly what the owner of this Cadillac Escalade wanted. One day, he took his full-size SUV to a tuner in Texas to surprise his wife. A couple of weeks later, he drove home in an 800-horsepower monster with good road manners and oomph enough to make other drivers at the stoplight wonder.
Scott was the one who brought in his wife's Cadillac Escalade all the way from Connecticut. This build is actually an early Christmas gift for his wife, Lauren. He bought it sight unseen and took it straight to a tuner in Katy, Texas, to have it transformed.
Finished in Argent Silver Metallic, an $825 option, the Escalade wears one of the rarest colors since most of them are sold in either black or white. However, the family plans to have it wrapped. It will happen when the missus chooses the color.
The Cadillac Escalade-V is a monster from the moment it rolls off the production line of the General Motors Arlington Assembly Plant in Arlington, Texas. It comes with the 6.2-liter supercharged V8, pumping out a massive 682 horsepower (691 metric horsepower) and 653 pound-feet (885 Newton meters) of torque.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube That is enough for the SUV to rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 4.4 seconds, despite playing in the heavyweight category at 6,217 pounds (2,820 kilograms), on its way to a top speed of 125 mph (201 kph).
However, all those figures are far behind. When it entered the shop, the Escalade-V baselined at 500 rear-wheel horsepower and 477 pound-feet of rear-wheel torque. Now, it is driving off with 644 rear-wheel horsepower, which translates to roughly 800 at the crank, and 587 pound-feet of torque. Late Model Racecraft ’s 800 HP Package is to blame for the extra oomph.
The Escalade-V got a larger throttle body, a custom elbow, an S&B cold air induction system, and a tuned ECM, but it retains the stock supercharger, fully ported and getting more airflow. Also factory are the headers, manifolds, and exhaust. This makes it still idle and drive like it did the day it left the factory, but with a solid horsepower gain.
Lauren won't even know the difference until she steps on it. Now, in V Mode, her brand-newCadillac Escalade-V acts and sounds like a Chevy Corvette. She is definitely going to notice that!
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube Steven Fereday takes the SUV for a spin to make sure he is delivering a reliable vehicle and is sure that Scott will probably drive it more than his missus. Each acceleration puts a smile on his face. It is probably going to have the same effect on Lauren and Scott.
Scott jumped into the comments section to tell LMR that he will ship his C6 Chevy Corvette ZR1 to them for an upgrade.
